cells.tense: You are open now, and nothing has to be decided yet.
cells.ask: Name one thing you feel today, to yourself, and leave it unnamed to anyone else until tomorrow.
cells.core:
Something's coming toward you and you haven't closed the door on it. Feelings arrive before you know what they're about, and right now that's fine with you — you don't have to file each one under a name or a plan. You notice what lands. You let it land.

The pull of the possible is alive in you, and it hasn't turned into grabbing. What you feel stays yours while it stays open, which is a harder trick than it sounds — most people either shut the door or rush the guest in. You can let one thing stay unnamed for a day, and see what it becomes when nothing hurries it.
cells.sheetLine: You're open to what's arriving, and you haven't rushed to name it.
cells.verb: letting what's entering be felt before it's named
cells.place: at the threshold where the next thing arrives

cells.tense: You're bracing for what's coming before it has arrived.
cells.ask: Pick one thing you're waiting on and write down what you'd choose if it didn't come.
cells.core:
You've already decided what's coming, and how much it will cost, and what you'll have to do about it. None of that has happened yet. The future got written before it got here, and now you're standing at the door rehearsing a scene the day hasn't asked of you.

Openness in you has turned into a scan for what might hurt. You read the moment for what it might demand and you get there ahead of it, so nothing reaches you fresh — it reaches you already answered. The cost isn't that you feel too much. It's that the door is being held shut against things that haven't knocked. There's a way to want something without needing to control what comes.

cells.tense: You meet what's arriving with the door half shut, watching from a step back.
cells.ask: Answer one thing honestly today when someone asks what you feel — the first word, uncorrected.
cells.core:
Something's arriving and you're not in the room for it. Not resisting, not judging — just not there when the thing lands. The heart that used to open at newness is quieter now, and you've stopped expecting it to open at all.

What's gone isn't feeling and it isn't willingness. It's the current that used to carry what came in to where you live. Watch what happens when a moment asks you something small — a friend's question, a song, a first look at the day — and see whether anything moves. Nothing needs forcing into the still spot. What's needed is contact with something fresh, and the way back through is showing up again, even flat, even saying so.
cells.sheetLine: What's arriving is here, and you're not there to meet it.
cells.verb: letting what's entering be felt before it's named
cells.place: at the threshold where the next thing arrives

cells.tense: You are already letting things in, and calling none of it your doing.
cells.ask: Say out loud, once, that one thing you felt today was yours to feel, and let someone else have theirs.
cells.core:
Things are getting in. You react, you soften, you're moved by what happens around you — and you describe it as if the day did it to you. The door is open and working. You just haven't signed for it.

The give-and-take is running in both directions and you're carrying only the receiving half as if it happened on its own. Somebody said something and it stayed with you. You felt what they felt before you knew you were feeling it. That's yours. Owning one moment like that, plainly, out loud, gives the rest of the day its proper address — one thing arrived, one thing was yours to feel, and you got to name it. Once is enough, and the other person keeps theirs.
